thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Incident opened (INC-1767): sudden spike of scraper/bot traffic hitting /v1/embeddings and batch endpoints, elevated 429/503 from edge. Observed 10x baseline RPS from many short-lived API keys. First seen 2026-03-15T02:54:48Z.

nina: ack — I'm oncall. Triage starting. Noting a lot of identical user-agent patterns across requests.

liam: pulling WAF and edge logs now, running histogram on UA and X-Forwarded-For. quick grep shows repeated UAs: "Go-http-client/1.1", "python-requests/2.31", and a few weird 1-char UAs.

liam: logs indicate fanout from many proxied IPs via same ASN (candidate ASN 46606). lots of short streams, tiny sequences.

sarah: recommended immediate mitigations: 1) per-key rate-slicing to 20 req/min (embeds) 2) WAF rule to block UA regex (temporary) 3) enable geo-throttle for high-volume source ASNs. Ready to apply once nina gives go.

nina: go ahead. I'll coordinate customer impact windows. Executing now:
```
# Apply per-key rate limit
edgectl routes update /v1/embeddings --per_key_rate 20/m
# Add temporary WAF rule (ua regex)
wafctl rules add --scope edge --name "suspicious-ua-block" --match "ua:(Go-http-client|python-requests|curl)" --action block
```

liam: confirmed WAF rule rolled to canary (us-east-1) by deploy-bot. seeing immediate drop in bot traffic on canary. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: canary deploy succeeded (rule:suspicious-ua-block) — 1 minute ago.

nina: rolling global now. Noting some legitimate customers use curl for healthchecks — devon please check for false positives.

devon: looking through support logs — 8 tickets started around 02:55Z. Quick list: org-alpha (embed prod jobs failing), org-beta (batch rerank 500s), org-gamma (sporadic 429s, low volume). I'll file a priority note and open interim TTL exemptions for org-alpha and org-beta while we investigate.

liam: after global WAF + per-key rate-slice, overall RPS dropped ~65%. Error rate on /v1/embeddings 5xx down from 18% -> 3% in 6m. However, we see increased 429s for a handful of high-throughput customers (likely throttled by new slice).

sarah: issuing temporary quota bump to avoid customer-impact for org-alpha and org-beta (applied only to their org-ids):
```
quotactl update --org org-alpha --embeddings_rate 200/m --expires 2026-03-15T05:00:00Z
quotactl update --org org-beta --embeddings_rate 150/m --expires 2026-03-15T05:00:00Z
```

kevin: security recs: block known bad ASN ranges at the edge, add header fingerprinting for proxy indicators, and sinkhole traffic with fake 200s for aggressive scrapers to waste their cycles. Propose ASN block + UA block + X-Proxy fingerprint rule.

liam: ASN block test applied to us-east (deny ASN 46606) — immediate reduction in fanout. Testing false-positive risk: none observed in canary so far.

nina: summary for exec/status: incident caused by distributed scraper/proxy farm using many short-lived keys and generic UAs; impact: elevated latency and 5xx for embeddings and batch endpoints across multiple regions, ~8 customer tickets, top 2 affected customers temporarily quota-bumped. Current state: mitigations applied (per-key rate-slice, UA WAF rule, ASN block), traffic down to ~140% baseline (was 600%).

devon: sending proactive status to affected customers now with templated note: "We've applied temporary protections to prevent abusive traffic; you may see reduced throughput — we're authorizing temporary quota increases for affected customers and will follow up once stabilised." Will attach link to status page.

nina: next steps: 1) handoff to michael at 09:30 PST (30m) 2) create postmortem stub + collect p95 token latency graphs 3) evaluation: implement header fingerprint + UA whitelisting in runbook 4) consider rolling out small cache for repeated embed prefixes.

michael: taking over at 09:30 PST. I'll watch the dashboards and continue mitigations. If traffic rebounds, escalate to a full network-level drop.

kevin: noted follow-ups for sec: build automated ASN detection playbook, integrate UA fingerprint into risk scoring, and add automated sinkhole (return 200 + slow body) for aggressive scrapers to reduce CPU.

liam: small debug note — one of the attacker patterns injected the header `X-Requested-With: xmlhttprequest` consistently; adding that to detection rules reduces false positives over time.

nina: adding runbook entry now. runbook snippet: 
```
1) identify UA and ASN pattern via quickedge query
2) apply per-key slice 20/m
3) deploy WAF UA regex to canary, validate for 5m
4) if drop >= 50% -> roll global
5) quota-exempt top customers as needed
6) open support messages
7) handoff
```

ops-bot: Incident INC-1767 updated: mitigations applied; incident severity downgraded to S2.

michael: confirmed stability for handoff window, continuing monitoring until 12:00 PST. I'll own postmortem and coordinate with security + support for customer outreach.

nina: thanks team. Follow-ups: (1) postmortem with timeline and signal graphs, (2) implement UA/headers fingerprint detection, (3) add runbook automation for per-key slice and temporary quota bump for top-tier customers, (4) validate caching strategy for repeated embeddings. Closing thread for active paging, will reopen if new spike. :lock:"
